descriptionChirho: A feminine noun meaning 'gift' or 'present,' used in construct ('gift of') and absolute ('a gift') to denote something given freely, whether from God or between persons (Proverbs 18:16, 19:6, 21:14, 25:14; Ecclesiastes 3:13, 5:18). Multilingual glosses uniformly point to 'gift/present': English 'gift/a gift,' Spanish 'don de/un regalo,' Hindi 'dan/uphar' (दान/उपहार), Arabic 'atiyyah/hadiyyah' (عَطِيَّةُ/هَدِيَّةً), Korean 'seonmul' (선물), Swahili 'zawadi.' The two clusters differ only by construct state and prepositional prefix, not by semantic content.
